Making it feel organised is what people remember. A screen on the wall does most of that: it shows everyone the thing is being kept properly, and it gives the people who are resting somewhere to look.

It works for a competition that runs all winter too. Leave the table up on the clubhouse screen and the group sees it every time they walk past.

posts.caption:
Every group has one who won't download anything.

They can play anyway. The host types their name on the invite screen and they're in the rounds, with partners, opponents, courts and a place in the table.

The catch: nothing gets kept for them. No profile, so their matches, points and ELO are gone when the competition ends, and no chat from their own phone. Usually around week two they see somebody else's profile.

Swipe for how it works. Bring them anyway. Guests play for free, and so does everyone with an account.
